grammar.topic: Present simple and adverbs of frequency
grammar.concept: Use the present simple to talk about routines and habits. Use frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) to show how often actions happen.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم المضارع أيضاً لوصف العادات، لكن ترتيب كلمات التكرار قد يختلف (غالباً يوضع بعد الفعل). الأفعال تتغير بناءً على الضمائر في العربية أيضاً.
grammar.structure: Subject + (adverb of frequency) + main verb (e.g. I usually drink water). For the verb to be: Subject + be + (adverb) (e.g. She is always tired). For negatives use do/does + not + verb.
grammar.commonError: Placing the adverb after the main verb (I go sometimes to the park) or using do/does with 'be' (She does not is).
grammar.exampleEN: I often go for a walk. He doesn't drink coffee. She is usually busy in the morning.
grammar.exampleAR: أنا غالباً أذهب للمشي. هو لا يشرب القهوة. هي عادةً مشغولة في الصباح.

readingBrief: A short original passage (about 130–160 words) that follows one person's simple daily routine and small wellbeing habits. The text describes morning and evening actions (wake up early, have breakfast, drink water, go for a walk), uses present simple and several adverbs of frequency (always, usually, sometimes, never), and mentions one habit the person wants to change. The passage is clear, learner-friendly, and gives a small personal detail to invite learners to compare with their own routines.
writingPrompt: Write a short message (60–90 words) to your English teacher describing your daily routine and one habit you want to start or stop. Include at least three frequency words (always, usually, sometimes, never, often) and one time (e.g. 7:00 or in the evening). Purpose: to explain your routine and set a simple goal. Audience: your teacher.

vocabulary.definition: a greater amount
vocabulary.exampleEN: I have more energy after sleeping well.

vocabulary.definition: improve or become better over time

vocabulary.exampleAR: بالممارسة، سيتحسن نطقك.

grammar.concept: Use comparatives to say how two things are different (e.g., smaller, more comfortable). Use the present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) to talk about actions happening now or changes that are in progress.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستعمل أحيانًا صيغة المضارع مع كلمات مثل الآن أو ما زال للتعبير عن الفعل الجاري. أما في الإنجليزية فنستخدم am/is/are + الفعل مع -ing للزمن المستمر، ونستخدم -er أو more + صفة للمقارنة.
grammar.structure: Comparative: adjective + -er + than (short adjectives) or more + adjective + than (long adjectives). Present continuous: subject + am/is/are + verb(-ing). Example combined: 'She is getting faster than before.'
grammar.commonError: Students often say 'more better' or forget to use -ing with the present continuous (e.g., 'I am improve' instead of 'I am improving'). Also check irregular comparatives (good → better).
grammar.exampleEN: Short comparative: 'This exam is easier than the last one.' Present continuous: 'I am studying more each week.' Combined: 'My reading is getting better than last month.'
grammar.exampleAR: مقارنة قصيرة: 'هذا الاختبار أسهل من السابق.' الزمن المستمر: 'أنا أدرس أكثر كل أسبوع.' مزيج: 'قرائتي تتحسن عن الشهر الماضي.'

readingBrief: A 130–160-word passage about Maria, who makes small lifestyle changes over three months. The text shows step-by-step adjustments: she sets a goal, takes small steps, and tracks progress. It uses comparatives (e.g., 'It is easier than I thought') and present continuous verbs to show ongoing change (e.g., 'I am walking more'). The passage includes simple time markers (last month, now, every week) and practical details (sleep, short walks, study time). Learners will find clear examples of comparatives and continuous actions in everyday contexts to model their own sentences.
writingPrompt: Write 60–90 words to a friend describing one small change you are making and the progress you see. Use at least one comparative (e.g., more, less, -er) and one present continuous sentence (I am ...ing). Say your goal and ask a short question for advice. Audience: a friend. Purpose: share progress and ask for help or tips.

grammar.arabicName: الأسماء المعدودة وغير المعدودة؛ أدوات الكمية
grammar.concept: Countable nouns have plural forms (apple, apples). Uncountable nouns do not usually have a plural form (rice, milk). Use different quantifiers: many/few with countable; much/a little with uncountable; some/any with both in positive/negative/questions.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية يوجد جمع للأسماء المعدودة وزمن الجمع، وللكميات تستخدم كلمات مثل 'قليل' و'قليل من' و'بعض'. هنا نستخدم 'many' مع المعدودات و'much' مع غير المعدودات، بينما 'some' و'any' تستخدم مع النوعين.
grammar.structure: Positive: many + plural countable (many apples). much + uncountable (much rice). some + plural/uncountable (some vegetables, some water). Negative/questions: any (Do you have any milk?). a few (positive, countable), a little (positive, uncountable).
grammar.commonError: Learners often use 'much' with countable nouns (much apples) or forget plural forms (one apple, two apple). Another error is using 'a few' for uncountable nouns instead of 'a little'.
grammar.exampleEN: I have a few apples. / I have a little rice. / Do you have any milk? / She eats many vegetables.
grammar.exampleAR: لدي قليل من التفاحات. / لدي قليل من الأرز. / هل لديك أي حليب؟ / هي تأكل الكثير من الخضروات.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original passage describing one person's weekday meals and energy levels. The text explains what they eat for breakfast, lunch and a small snack, using countable and uncountable nouns with simple quantifiers (a glass of, a slice of, a few, a little, some). writingPrompt: Write 60–90 words to a friend describing your typical lunch and one snack this week. Purpose: share information and a simple opinion.

vocabulary.exampleEN: After work, she relaxes with music.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد العمل، تسترخي مع الموسيقى.

vocabulary.definition: something that is more important than other things
vocabulary.exampleEN: Family is my top priority this weekend.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الأسرة هي أولويتي الكبرى هذا الأسبوع.

vocabulary.definition: used to show a preference for one thing instead of another
vocabulary.exampleEN: I will read a book rather than watch TV.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأقرأ كتابًا بدلًا من مشاهدة التلفاز.

vocabulary.definition: on some occasions but not always
vocabulary.exampleEN: Sometimes I go to the gym in the morning.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحيانًا أذهب إلى الصالة الرياضية في الصباح.

vocabulary.definition: during Saturday and Sunday
vocabulary.exampleEN: We visit our grandparents at the weekend.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نزور أجدادنا في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.

grammar.concept: Use 'like' for general preferences, 'would like' for a specific wish or polite request, and 'prefer' to compare two or more options.
grammar.arabicComparison: تستخدم «like» للتعبير عن التفضيل العام، «would like» للرغبة المحددة أو الطلب المهذب، و«prefer» للمقارنة بين خيارين أو أكثر.
grammar.structure: Like: I like + noun / I like + -ing. Would like: I would like to + base verb. Question: Would you like to + verb? Prefer: I prefer + noun / I prefer + -ing / I prefer X to Y.
grammar.commonError: Mixing 'like' and 'would like' (e.g. saying 'I like to a coffee' instead of 'I would like a coffee') and forgetting to use -ing after 'prefer' when comparing activities (e.g. 'I prefer play' instead of 'I prefer playing').
grammar.exampleEN: I like cycling. I would like to try cycling in the countryside. I prefer cycling to running.
grammar.exampleAR: أحب ركوب الدراجة. أودّ تجربة ركوب الدراجة في الريف. أفضل ركوب الدراجة على الركض.

readingBrief: A short 130–160-word first-person passage about planning a weekend. The writer lists two or three hobbies (for example: reading, walking, watching films), explains how they make time for activities, and describes a choice between meeting friends or staying home with family. The text uses simple time words (tomorrow, at the weekend), and examples of like, would like, and prefer. It shows reasons for a decision (time, cost, family) and ends with a clear plan for Saturday or Sunday.
writingPrompt: Write an email (60–90 words) to a friend to explain your plans for the weekend. Say what you like doing in your free time, what you would like to try, and which activity you prefer and why. The audience is a friend; the purpose is to make a plan and explain your priorities.

title: People who help us

outcome.canDo: I can describe people who help me using adjectives and a basic relative clause.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف الأشخاص الذين يساعدونني باستخدام الصفات وجملة وصفية بسيطة.
outcome.scenario: You will talk about helpers at home, school and in the neighbourhood and say why they are important.
outcome.scenarioArabic: ستتحدث عن الأشخاص الذين يساعدونك في البيت والمدرسة وفي الحي وتقول لماذا هم مهمون.

retrieval.prompt: What time did you meet a friend yesterday? Where did you go?
retrieval.purpose: Activate simple past with time and places (yesterday, time, go).

retrieval.prompt: Who can help you if you want advice about food or health?
retrieval.purpose: Recall people and simple verbs (want, can, people, food).

retrieval.prompt: Do you like to ask your family for help or a neighbour? Why?
retrieval.purpose: Use basic verbs and people vocabulary (like, ask, family, neighbour).

retrieval.prompt: Can you go to the doctor tomorrow or do you want to call first?
retrieval.purpose: Practice modal can and simple future idea (tomorrow, want, call).

network.learningNote: Focus on easy adjectives (kind, patient, reliable) and form one short relative clause with who/that. Encourage students to keep adjective order simple: opinion before noun.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركز على صفات بسيطة (لطيف، صبور، موثوق) وصغ جملة وصفية واحدة بسيطة ب who/that. شجّع الطلاب على وضع الصفات قبل الاسم.

vocabulary.definition: A person who cares for sick people in a hospital or clinic.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The nurse checks the patient's temperature.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تفحص الممرضة حرارة المريض.

vocabulary.definition: A person who lives near your home.
vocabulary.exampleEN: My neighbour helped me carry my bags.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعدني جاري في حمل الحقائب.

vocabulary.definition: A trained person who helps people with problems in life and family.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The social worker visits families who need support.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يزور العامل الاجتماعي الأسر التي تحتاج إلى دعم.

vocabulary.definition: To tell someone what you think they should do.
vocabulary.exampleEN: My teacher gives advice about studying.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يقدّم معلمي نصائح عن المذاكرة.

vocabulary.definition: Help or assistance when someone needs it.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Friends can give emotional support.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكن للأصدقاء تقديم الدعم العاطفي.

vocabulary.definition: Showing kindness and concern for others.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She is a caring person who listens carefully.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هي شخص مُهتم يستمع بعناية.

vocabulary.definition: Someone you can trust to do what they say.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He is reliable; he arrives on time.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هو شخص موثوق؛ يصل في الوقت المحدد.

vocabulary.definition: Police, ambulance, and fire services for urgent help.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Call the emergency services in serious accidents.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اتصل بخدمات الطوارئ في الحوادث الخطيرة.

vocabulary.definition: To take care of someone or something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Can you look after my cat while I am away?
vocabulary.exampleAR: هل يمكنك الاعتناء بقطتي أثناء غيابي؟

vocabulary.definition: A person in your family (mother, father, sister…).
vocabulary.exampleEN: A family member can help with childcare.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكن لأحد أفراد العائلة المساعدة في رعاية الأطفال.

vocabulary.definition: A person receiving medical care.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The patient waited for the doctor.
vocabulary.exampleAR: انتظر المريض الطبيب.

vocabulary.definition: To pay attention to what someone says.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Good helpers listen to people's problems.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المساعدون الجيدون يستمعون لمشكلات الآخرين.

vocabulary.definition: To believe someone will do what they promise / the belief itself.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I trust my friend to keep my secret.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أثق بصديقي أن يحتفظ بسرّي.

vocabulary.definition: Willing to help and useful.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The librarian is helpful when I search for books.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المكتبي مفيد عندما أبحث عن كتب.

vocabulary.definition: To ask for urgent help, often in an emergency.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If there is a fire, call for help immediately.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا كان هناك حريق، اطلب المساعدة فوراً.

grammar.concept: Use adjectives before nouns to describe people (a kind friend). Use a simple relative clause with who/that to add information about a person: The teacher who helps me is patient.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم أداة الوصل مثل الذي/التي بعد الاسم (مثال: المعلم الذي يساعدني). في الإنجليزية تكون الصفة قبل الاسم، أما الجملة الوصفية فتستخدم who/that بعد الاسم.
grammar.structure: Adjective + noun: a kind neighbour.   Noun + relative clause: the neighbour who helps me / the person that I trust.
grammar.commonError: Placing the adjective after the noun (e.g. 'a neighbour kind') or omitting the relative pronoun in formal speech. A common learner error is to use Arabic word order for adjectives.
grammar.exampleEN: The doctor who works at the clinic is reliable. She is a caring doctor.
grammar.exampleAR: الطبيب الذي يعمل في العيادة موثوق. إنها طبيبة عطوفة.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original passage describing three people who help in a small community: a nurse at the health centre, a neighbour who looks after an elderly person, and a volunteer who organises food for families. The text uses simple adjectives (kind, reliable, busy) and includes one or two basic relative clauses with who/that. Learners practise reading for specific information (who does what) and notice the adjectives and the structure of the short relative clauses.
writingPrompt: Write a short message (60–90 words) to a friend describing one person who helps you in your life (for example a teacher, neighbour or family member). Say three adjectives about them and include one relative clause with who or that (for example: who helps me). Purpose: to describe and thank the person. Audience: your friend.

title: A neighbourhood worth knowing

outcome.canDo: I can say what is in a neighbourhood and give simple places and directions using there is/are and place prepositions.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أقول ما يوجد في الحي وأن أعطي أماكن واتجاهات بسيطة باستخدام there is/are وحروف جر المكان.
outcome.scenario: You meet a new neighbour and tell them where the shops and services are and how to get to the bus stop and park.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تلتقي بجار جديد وتخبره أين تقع المتاجر والخدمات وكيف يصل إلى موقف الحافلات والحديقة.

retrieval.prompt: Tell your partner: Where did you go yesterday? Where will you go tomorrow?
retrieval.purpose: Activate simple past/future time words and short answers.

retrieval.prompt: Name three places in your town you like and say why.
retrieval.purpose: Recall common places and give short reasons.

retrieval.prompt: Ask a classmate: Can you show me the way to the nearest shop?
retrieval.purpose: Practice asking for help with simple modal can.

retrieval.prompt: Say what food you want to buy at the supermarket this week.
retrieval.purpose: Use simple shopping vocabulary and want + noun.

network.learningNote: Focus on there is/are for saying what exists, and simple prepositions (in, on, next to, behind, between, at) to show where things are. Use short natural phrases for directions like 'go straight' and 'turn left.' Practise matching singular/plural with there is/are.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركز على there is/are لبيان ما يوجد وحروف الجر البسيطة (in، on، next to، behind، between، at) لتحديد أماكن الأشياء. استخدم عبارات قصيرة وطبيعية للإتجاهات مثل 'go straight' و 'turn left'. مرن على مطابقة المفرد والجمع مع there is/are.

vocabulary.exampleEN: My neighbourhood has a small park and two shops.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حيّي يحتوي على حديقة صغيرة ومتجرين.

vocabulary.definition: the main part of a town with shops and offices
vocabulary.exampleEN: The city centre is busy on Saturdays.

vocabulary.exampleEN: Children play in the park after school.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يلعب الأطفال في الحديقة بعد المدرسة.

vocabulary.definition: a place to send letters and buy stamps

vocabulary.exampleAR: كن حذراً عند عبور الشارع المزدحم.

vocabulary.definition: a calm road with little traffic

grammar.topic: there is / there are and place prepositions
grammar.arabicName: There is / There are وحروف الجر للمكان
grammar.concept: Use there is for one thing and there are for more than one. Use prepositions (in, on, at, next to, behind, between, in front of, on the corner) to say where something is.
grammar.arabicComparison: في الإنجليزية نستخدم there is/there are للقول بوجود شيء، بينما في العربية نستخدم 'يوجد' أو 'هناك'. حروف الجر مثل in، on، next to تقابل في العربية في، على، بجوار.
grammar.structure: There is + singular noun / There are + plural noun. Negative: There isn't / There aren't. Short answer: Yes, there is. No, there aren't. Preposition examples: in the park, on the corner, next to the shop, behind the library, between the bank and the café.
grammar.commonError: Using 'there is' with plural nouns (wrong: There is two shops). Choosing the wrong preposition (wrong: The bus stop is in the corner → correct: on the corner).
grammar.exampleEN: There is a café next to the library. There are two banks on the high street.
grammar.exampleAR: هناك مقهى بجوار المكتبة. يوجد مصرفان في الشارع الرئيسي.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word friendly guide written by a local resident describing one neighbourhood. The short passage lists five key places (park, supermarket, library, café, post office), mentions approximate locations with prepositions (next to, on the corner, behind), and gives two short directions using 'go straight' and 'turn left'. The text uses several examples of there is/there are and highlights opening times (open late). The tone is informal and useful for a new neighbour.
writingPrompt: Write a 60–90-word note to a new neighbour to tell them about three helpful places in your area (for example: supermarket, bus stop, park) and give simple directions using there is/are and place prepositions. Audience: new neighbour. Purpose: help them find places and invite them to meet for a walk.

title: Getting there

outcome.canDo: I can ask and give simple directions and talk about short journeys using buses, trains and walking.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أطلب وأعطي اتجاهات بسيطة وأتحدث عن رحلات قصيرة بالحافلة والقطار والمشي.
outcome.scenario: You arrive in a new neighbourhood and need to explain to a friend how to get to the café and the station.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تصل إلى حي جديد وتحتاج أن تشرح لصديق كيف يصل إلى المقهى والمحطة.

retrieval.prompt: What time do you usually go to work or class?
retrieval.purpose: Recall common time words and 'go' in sentences.

retrieval.prompt: Name three places you like in your town (for example: shop, park, school).
retrieval.purpose: Activate A1 place vocabulary to connect with transport.

retrieval.prompt: Who can help you if you are lost? (person or place)
retrieval.purpose: Use simple people words (friend, police, receptionist) in a travel context.

retrieval.prompt: What did you do yesterday? Use 'went' once.
retrieval.purpose: Practice past-time language and movement verbs in a short sentence.

network.learningNote: Teach imperatives with clear gestures and simple maps. Use short, natural commands (Turn left. Go straight on.) Practise positive and negative imperatives and show how prepositions (at, next to, opposite) work in short direction phrases.
network.learningNoteArabic: علّم الأوامر بصور واضحة وخرائط بسيطة. استخدم أوامر قصيرة وطبيعية (انعطف يسارًا. اذهب مباشرة). درّب الأوامر الموجبة والسالبة وأوضح كيف تعمل حروف الجر (عند، بجانب، أمام) في عبارات الاتجاه القصيرة.

vocabulary.definition: the place where a bus stops to pick up or drop off people
vocabulary.exampleEN: Wait at the bus stop near the corner.
vocabulary.exampleAR: انتظر في موقف الحافلة قرب الزاوية.

vocabulary.definition: to go onto a bus, train, or other vehicle
vocabulary.exampleEN: We get on the train at nine o'clock.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نصعد القطار في الساعة التاسعة.

vocabulary.definition: to leave a bus, train, or other vehicle
vocabulary.exampleEN: Get off at the second stop.
vocabulary.exampleAR: انزل عند المحطة الثانية.

vocabulary.arabic: غيّر القطار / قم بالتبديل بين القطارات
vocabulary.definition: to leave one train and travel on another to continue a journey
vocabulary.exampleEN: You must change trains at Central Station.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب أن تغيّر القطار في المحطة المركزية.

vocabulary.definition: a paper or electronic pass that allows you to travel on transport
vocabulary.exampleEN: Buy a ticket before you get on the bus.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اشترِ تذكرة قبل أن تصعد الحافلة.

vocabulary.definition: the money you pay to travel on public transport
vocabulary.exampleEN: The bus fare is cheaper in the morning.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أجرة الحافلة أرخص في الصباح.

vocabulary.definition: a raised area at a station where passengers get on or off trains
vocabulary.exampleEN: The train to Bristol leaves from platform 4.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يغادر القطار إلى بريستول من الرصيف رقم 4.

vocabulary.definition: a drawing that shows streets and places to help you find a way
vocabulary.exampleEN: Open the map to find the café.
vocabulary.exampleAR: افتح الخريطة لتجد المقهى.

vocabulary.definition: to continue in the same direction without turning
vocabulary.exampleEN: Go straight on for two blocks, then turn right.
vocabulary.exampleAR: امشِ مباشرة لمسافتين، ثم انعطف يمينًا.

vocabulary.definition: to change direction to the left
vocabulary.exampleEN: Turn left at the traffic lights.
vocabulary.exampleAR: انعطف يسارًا عند إشارة المرور.

vocabulary.definition: to change direction to the right
vocabulary.exampleEN: Turn right after the shop.
vocabulary.exampleAR: انعطف يمينًا بعد المتجر.

vocabulary.definition: a short distance away, just after the next turn
vocabulary.exampleEN: The bakery is just around the corner.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المخبز بجوار الزاوية مباشرة.

vocabulary.definition: the path or road you follow to get from one place to another
vocabulary.exampleEN: This route takes you along the river.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هذا المسار يأخذك على طول النهر.

vocabulary.definition: the act of travelling from one place to another
vocabulary.exampleEN: The journey to the station takes twenty minutes by foot.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تستغرق الرحلة إلى المحطة عشرين دقيقة سيرًا على الأقدام.

vocabulary.definition: to get on the bus that comes after the current one
vocabulary.exampleEN: If you miss this one, take the next bus.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا فاتتك هذه، استقل الحافلة التالية.

grammar.concept: Use the base verb to give short commands (imperatives) and combine them with simple direction phrases (go straight on, turn left) and prepositions (at, next to, opposite) to tell someone how to get somewhere.
grammar.arabicComparison: في الإنجليزية نستخدم الفعل في صورته الأساسية للأوامر (اِذهب، انعطف) بينما في العربية نستخدم صيغة فعل الأمر. جهز الطالب للتعرف على الاختلاف في ترتيب الكلمات ووجود حروف الجر بالإنجليزية مثل 'at' و'next to'.
grammar.structure: Imperative: [Base verb] + [direction phrase]. Examples: 'Turn left.' 'Go straight on.' 'Don't run.' For locations: '[Place] is [preposition] the [landmark].' Example: 'The café is next to the bank.'
grammar.commonError: Learners often add 'to' after the base verb (say 'to go straight' instead of 'go straight') or forget prepositions ('the café next the bank' instead of 'next to the bank').
grammar.exampleEN: Turn left at the lights, then go straight on. The station is opposite the library.
grammar.exampleAR: انعطف يسارًا عند الإشارات، ثم امشِ مباشرة. المحطة مقابل المكتبة.

readingBrief: A short, 130–160-word passage describing a simple trip across town. The text follows a young visitor who gets off a train, checks a small map, and walks to a café. It includes clear direction phrases (turn left, go straight on, around the corner), transport words (train, bus, platform, ticket) and a short exchange asking for help. The passage models imperatives and polite questions (Excuse me, where is ...? Can you tell me?), uses present and simple past verbs, and finishes with the speaker arriving at the café and describing the view. The tone is practical and friendly for A2 readers.
writingPrompt: Audience: a friend who will visit your neighbourhood. Purpose: write 60–90 words giving simple directions from the station to your favourite café. Include one transport word, two direction phrases (e.g. turn left, go straight on), and a short polite sentence offering help if needed.

vocabulary.definition: To tell the hotel you have arrived and get your room key
vocabulary.exampleEN: We checked in at 3 pm and went to our room.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قمنا بتسجيل الوصول الساعة الثالثة وذهبنا إلى غرفتنا.

vocabulary.definition: To pay and leave the hotel at the end of your stay
vocabulary.exampleEN: Please check out before 11 am.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يرجى تسجيل المغادرة قبل الساعة الحادية عشرة صباحًا.

vocabulary.definition: A card used to open a hotel room door
vocabulary.exampleEN: The receptionist gave me a new key card.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعطاني موظف الاستقبال بطاقة غرفة جديدة.

vocabulary.definition: A room with its own private bathroom
vocabulary.exampleEN: We chose a room with an ensuite bathroom.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اخترنا غرفة بها حمام داخلي.

vocabulary.definition: A room for one person
vocabulary.exampleEN: He booked a single room for one night.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حجز غرفة مفردة لليلة واحدة.

vocabulary.definition: A room for two people, usually with one double bed or two single beds
vocabulary.exampleEN: We stayed in a double room with a nice view.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أقمنا في غرفة مزدوجة بإطلالة جميلة.

vocabulary.definition: Sheets and covers for a bed
vocabulary.exampleEN: The bed linen looked clean and fresh.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بدا أن أغطية السرير نظيفة ومنتعشة.

vocabulary.definition: Making a lot of sound; not quiet
vocabulary.exampleEN: The street was noisy at night and I could not sleep.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كان الشارع صاخبًا في الليل ولم أستطع النوم.

vocabulary.definition: A device that makes a room warm
vocabulary.exampleEN: Please turn on the heater; it is very cold.
vocabulary.exampleAR: من فضلك شغّل السخان؛ الجو بارد جدًا.

vocabulary.definition: Water or liquid coming through where it should not
vocabulary.exampleEN: There is a leak under the sink in my bathroom.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك تسرب تحت الحوض في حمامي.

vocabulary.definition: The code you use to connect to the hotel's internet
vocabulary.exampleEN: May I have the Wi-Fi password, please?
vocabulary.exampleAR: هل أستطيع الحصول على كلمة مرور الواي فاي، من فضلك؟

vocabulary.definition: To ask for something you need or want
vocabulary.exampleEN: I will make a request for extra towels.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأقدم طلبًا لمناشف إضافية.

vocabulary.definition: To repair something that is broken
vocabulary.exampleEN: The staff will fix the heater this afternoon.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سيقوم الموظفون بإصلاح السخان هذا الظهر.

grammar.arabicName: استخدام can و could لطلب المساعدة
grammar.concept: Use can for informal requests and could for more polite or formal requests. Both forms ask someone to do something. 'Could' is softer and often better with strangers or staff.
grammar.arabicComparison: نستخدم can للطلبات العادية مع الأصدقاء، و could عندما نريد أن نكون أكثر مؤدبين، خاصة مع أشخاص لا نعرفهم أو الموظفين.
grammar.structure: Can / Could + subject + verb (base form)? + please (optional).
grammar.commonError: Students say 'Can you to fix the heater?' — do not use 'to' after can/could. Also avoid using could for past ability (different meaning).
grammar.exampleEN: Can you help me with the Wi-Fi? / Could you please change my room?
grammar.exampleAR: هل يمكنك مساعدتي في الواي فاي؟ / هل يمكنك من فضلك تغيير غرفتي؟

readingBrief: A 130–160-word passage describing a short stay at a small guesthouse. The guest explains checking in at reception, asking for the Wi‑Fi password, and reporting two problems: a noisy street and a slow shower with low hot water. The text shows a short dialogue with the receptionist who says they can move the guest to another room or send someone to fix the shower. It highlights polite requests using can and could, and gives simple reactions for the guest (thank you, that helps). The passage models useful phrases students can use when they stay somewhere new.
writingPrompt: Write a short email (60–90 words) to the hotel reception. Audience: hotel reception. Purpose: politely ask to change to a quieter room because your current room is noisy at night and to request a late check-out at 1 pm. Use can or could for your requests and include a thank you.

title: Shopping with a purpose

outcome.canDo: I can compare products and explain why I will buy something using too/enough and simple comparisons.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع مقارنة المنتجات وشرح سبب شرائي باستخدام too / enough والمقارنات البسيطة.
outcome.scenario: You need to buy one item for a clear purpose (e.g., a warm coat, a school bag, a phone). You make a short list, compare options, and decide within a budget.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تحتاج إلى شراء سلعة لغرض واضح (مثل معطف دافئ أو حقيبة مدرسية أو هاتف). تكتب قائمة قصيرة، تقارن الخيارات، وتقرر ضمن ميزانية.

retrieval.prompt: What did you buy yesterday?
retrieval.purpose: Warm-up: recall shopping vocabulary and past events.

retrieval.prompt: Where do you usually go for food or clothes?
retrieval.purpose: Activate places and routine vocabulary relevant to shopping.

retrieval.prompt: How much money do you have for a small purchase today?
retrieval.purpose: Use numbers and money language to prepare for budgeting.

retrieval.prompt: Can you pay by card or do you need cash?
retrieval.purpose: Prompt use of payment vocabulary in a real context.

network.anchor: Choose a product that fits your need and budget
network.learningNote: Focus on simple comparisons (X is cheaper than Y) and using too/enough to explain suitability. Encourage real choices (budget, purpose) rather than only vocabulary lists.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على المقارنات البسيطة (X أرخص من Y) واستخدام too / enough لشرح الملاءمة. شجّع الاختيارات الحقيقية (الميزانية، الهدف) بدلاً من قوائم كلمات فقط.

vocabulary.definition: not too expensive; you can pay for it
vocabulary.exampleEN: This coat is affordable for my budget.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هذا المعطف ميسور التكلفة بالنسبة لميزانيتي.

vocabulary.definition: a small label that shows how much something costs
vocabulary.exampleEN: Check the price tag before you decide.
vocabulary.exampleAR: افحص ملصق السعر قبل أن تقرر.

vocabulary.definition: a paper that shows what you bought and how much you paid
vocabulary.exampleEN: Keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.
vocabulary.exampleAR: احتفظ بالإيصال إذا احتجت إلى إرجاع السلعة.

vocabulary.definition: a reduction in the normal price
vocabulary.exampleEN: There is a 10% discount on school bags this week.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك خصم 10% على حقائب المدرسة هذا الأسبوع.

vocabulary.definition: something you buy for much less than usual
vocabulary.exampleEN: I found a bargain at the market.
vocabulary.exampleAR: وجدت صفقة جيدة في السوق.

vocabulary.definition: the company name of a product (e.g., a maker of clothes or phones)
vocabulary.exampleEN: I like this brand because it lasts longer.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحب هذه العلامة التجارية لأنها تدوم أطول.

vocabulary.definition: how good or well made something is
vocabulary.exampleEN: Good quality shoes may cost more but last longer.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الأحذية ذات الجودة الجيدة قد تكون أغلى لكنها تدوم أطول.

vocabulary.definition: strong and long-lasting
vocabulary.exampleEN: I need a durable bag for daily use.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحتاج حقيبة متينة للاستخدام اليومي.

vocabulary.definition: used before by someone else; not new
vocabulary.exampleEN: A second-hand phone can be a good way to save money.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الهاتف المستعمل قد يكون وسيلة جيدة لتوفير المال.

vocabulary.definition: available at a lower price than usual
vocabulary.exampleEN: The winter coats are on sale now.
vocabulary.exampleAR: معاطف الشتاء معروضة بسعرٍ مُنخفض الآن.

vocabulary.definition: to use a bank or credit card to pay
vocabulary.exampleEN: Can I pay by card, or is it cash only?
vocabulary.exampleAR: هل أستطيع الدفع بالبطاقة أم النقد فقط؟

vocabulary.definition: to put clothes on to see if they fit
vocabulary.exampleEN: I will try on the jacket before I buy it.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأجرب المعطف قبل أن أشتريه.

vocabulary.definition: the rules a shop has about returning items
vocabulary.exampleEN: Read the return policy in case the size is wrong.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اقرأ سياسة الإرجاع في حالة كان المقاس خاطئاً.

vocabulary.definition: worth the price; gives you what you need for the money
vocabulary.exampleEN: This phone is good value for students.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هذا الهاتف ذو قيمة جيدة للطلاب.

vocabulary.definition: the low and high amounts that a product can cost
vocabulary.exampleEN: Choose a laptop in your price range.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اختر حاسوباً محمولاً ضمن نطاق سعرك.

grammar.concept: Use comparatives to say which item is bigger/cheaper/more useful. Use 'too' to say something is not suitable and 'enough' to say something meets the need.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم كلمات مثل 'أكثر' أو إضافة صيغة التفضيل، وترتيب الكلمات يختلف. 'إنه كبير جدًا' مقابل 'كبير بما يكفي' تشابهان الاستخدام الإنجليزي لكن الترتيب يختلف.
grammar.structure: Comparatives: adjective + -er + than (cheaper than) OR more + adjective + than (more expensive than). Too/enough: too + adjective (too small); adjective + enough (big enough).
grammar.commonError: Students often say 'more cheaper' (wrong) or put 'enough' before a noun (wrong: 'enough money' is correct, but not 'money enough' in English).
grammar.exampleEN: This bag is cheaper than that one. The coat is too small. The coat is big enough for winter.
grammar.exampleAR: هذه الحقيبة أرخص من تلك. المعطف صغير جداً. المعطف كبير بما يكفي للشتاء.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word passage in simple English about a person who needs one specific item (a warm coat for a cold trip). The text shows three options: a cheap new coat, a more expensive high-quality coat, and a second-hand coat on sale. The writer compares price, quality, and durability, and uses comparatives and 'too'/'enough' to explain why they choose the middle option. The passage practices skimming for main idea, scanning for numbers and prices, and identifying comparative language.
writingPrompt: Write a 60–90 word email to a friend explaining what you plan to buy and why. Say what your budget is, compare two options (use one comparative) and use too or enough once. Ask your friend for short advice (one question). Audience: a friend. Purpose: get opinion and make a decision.

title: The people around you

outcome.canDo: I can describe people I know: their appearance and character, and give extra information using who/which/that clauses.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع وصف الأشخاص الذين أعرفهم: مظهرهم وشخصيتهم، وإعطاء معلومات إضافية باستخدام جمل الوصل who/which/that.
outcome.scenario: You write short descriptions of neighbours, friends and colleagues for a class profile board.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تكتب وصفاً قصيراً للجيران والأصدقاء والزملاء لملف تعريفي في الصف.

retrieval.prompt: Tell me about people you like. Use the words: like, can, want.
retrieval.purpose: Activate simple verbs and people vocabulary to prepare for descriptions.

retrieval.prompt: Say where you go on the weekend and name a person who goes with you (use 'who').
retrieval.purpose: Reuse places and people while practising the relative word who.

retrieval.prompt: Talk about what you did yesterday with a friend and what you will do tomorrow.
retrieval.purpose: Connect time words (yesterday, tomorrow) with people vocabulary.

retrieval.prompt: اكتب عن شخصٍ تعرفه: أين يذهب، ماذا يريد، ماذا يأكل (use simple A1 words like: مكان، طعام، يريد).
retrieval.purpose: تفعيل كلمات A1 في سياق وصف شخص.

chunks: have a good sense of humour
priorLevelLinks: A1: simple present questions and answers
network.learningNote: Focus on short relative clauses with who/which/that. Teach one clause at a time: start with people (who), then things (which/that). Use chunks like 'get on well with' in example sentences.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركِّز على جمل الوصل القصيرة باستخدام who للأشخاص و which/that للأشياء. علِّم جملة واحدة في كل مرة واستخدم تعابير مثل «get on well with» في أمثلة.

vocabulary.definition: a person who lives near you
vocabulary.exampleEN: My neighbour who lives next door is kind.
vocabulary.exampleAR: جارِي الذي يعيش بجانبنا لطيف.

vocabulary.definition: how someone looks to other people
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her appearance is friendly and tidy.
vocabulary.exampleAR: مظهرها ودود ومرتب.

vocabulary.definition: the way a person usually thinks and behaves
vocabulary.exampleEN: He has a calm character and he helps others.
vocabulary.exampleAR: له شخصية هادئة ويُساعد الآخرين.

vocabulary.definition: using more height than average
vocabulary.exampleEN: My cousin is tall and plays basketball.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ابن عمي طويل ويلعب كرة السلة.

vocabulary.definition: kind and pleasant to other people
vocabulary.exampleEN: The teacher is friendly and helpful.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المعلّم ودود ويعاون الطلاب.

vocabulary.definition: not loud; calm and not speaking much
vocabulary.exampleEN: Our neighbour is quiet but polite.
vocabulary.exampleAR: جارنا هادئ لكنه مؤدب.

vocabulary.definition: not comfortable talking to new people
vocabulary.exampleEN: She is shy at first but friendly later.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هي خجولة في البداية لكنها ودودة بعد ذلك.

vocabulary.definition: enjoying meeting and talking to people
vocabulary.exampleEN: An outgoing person likes to join events.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الشخص المنفتح يحب حضور الفعاليات.

vocabulary.definition: hair that has many small curves or ringlets
vocabulary.exampleEN: The woman who has curly hair works at the shop.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المرأة التي تملك شعرًا مجعدًا تعمل في المتجر.

vocabulary.word: have a good sense of humour
vocabulary.definition: to be good at making people laugh or see the funny side
vocabulary.exampleEN: I like my friend who has a good sense of humour.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحب صديقي الذي يتمتع بحس فكاهي جيد.

vocabulary.definition: a friend you trust and see often
vocabulary.exampleEN: Maria is a close friend who knows my family.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ماريا صديقة مقربة تعرف عائلتي.

vocabulary.definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
vocabulary.exampleEN: I get on well with the neighbours who help me.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أتفاهم مع الجيران الذين يساعدونني.

vocabulary.definition: short, polite conversation about simple topics
vocabulary.exampleEN: We made small talk with the new neighbour.
vocabulary.exampleAR: جرينا حديثًا بسيطًا مع الجار الجديد.

vocabulary.definition: someone you can trust to do what they say
vocabulary.exampleEN: He is reliable: he always arrives on time.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هو شخص يمكن الاعتماد عليه: يصل دائمًا في الموعد.

vocabulary.definition: to have the same appearance as someone or something
vocabulary.exampleEN: You look like your sister who lives in London.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تبدو مثل أختك التي تعيش في لندن.

grammar.concept: Use who for people and which/that for things to add extra information about a noun. The clause comes after the noun it describes. Keep clauses short at A2.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم الذي/التي/الذين لوصل المعلومات (مثلاً: الرجل الذي يساعدني). ترتيب الكلمات يختلف قليلاً لكن الفكرة نفسها: جملة تشرح الاسم.
grammar.structure: noun + who/which/that + subject + verb. Example patterns: 'a person who lives next door', 'a dog that barks'.
grammar.commonError: Using which for people (wrong) or leaving out the relative word in spoken A2 English. Also, do not add extra verbs: 'who he is' inside a noun phrase is often wrong.
grammar.exampleEN: My neighbour, who is kind, helps me with shopping. I have a bike that is blue.
grammar.exampleAR: جارِي، الذي لطيف، يساعدني في التسوق. لدي دراجة التي لونها أزرق.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original passage about three people in a small neighbourhood. The text introduces a neighbour, a shopkeeper and a friend, describing their appearance and character with simple present tense. It uses short relative clauses with who/which/that to give extra details (for example, 'the neighbour who helps us' and 'the shop which sells fresh bread'). The passage includes several target chunks (close friend, get on well with, small talk) and uses learner vocabulary from this lesson. Tone is friendly and clear, suitable for A2 readers who are practising description and relative clauses.
writingPrompt: Write 60–90 words to your teacher describing three people you know in your neighbourhood or community. Use who/which/that clauses to add details (for example: 'a neighbour who...'), and include at least two chunks from the lesson (for example: close friend, get on well with). Purpose: introduce these people and explain one thing you like or how you get on with them. / اكتب 60–90 كلمة إلى معلمك تصف فيها ثلاثة أشخاص تعرفهم في الحي أو المجتمع، واستخدم جمل الوصل who/which/that وعبارتين على الأقل من الدرس.

title: A day I will remember

outcome.canDo: I can tell a short story about an event in the past using past simple verbs and sequencing words.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أحكي قصة قصيرة عن حدث في الماضي باستخدام أفعال الماضي البسيط وكلمات ترتيب الأحداث.
outcome.scenario: You are telling a friend about a special day you will always remember (who was there, what happened, how you felt).
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تخبر صديقًا عن يوم مميز ستتذكره دائمًا (من كان هناك، ماذا حدث، وكيف شعرت).

retrieval.prompt: Tell me where you went yesterday and one thing you ate.
retrieval.purpose: Warm-up recall of time, places and food in the past.

retrieval.prompt: أخبرني عن شخص قابلته أمس وماذا فعلتما.
retrieval.purpose: تذكير بالمفردات الأساسية: people, go, do, yesterday.

retrieval.prompt: Say one place you like and why you like it (use like).
retrieval.purpose: Activate present likes to connect to past memories.

retrieval.prompt: اكتب جملة قصيرة عن طعام تحبه ومتى أكلته آخر مرة.
retrieval.purpose: تكرار كلمات الطعام والزمان: food, time, yesterday.

priorLevelLinks: use of past simple: I went, I saw (Module 2)
talking about time words: yesterday, last week (Module 1)
network.learningNote: Focus on sequencing words (first, then, after that, finally) to tell events clearly. Keep past verbs regular or irregular simple forms (went, saw, felt).
network.learningNoteArabic: ركز على كلمات ترتيب الأحداث (أولاً، ثم، بعد ذلك، أخيرًا) لسرد الأحداث بوضوح. استخدم أفعال الماضي البسيط بصيغ بسيطة (went, saw, felt).

vocabulary.definition: a thing that you remember from the past
vocabulary.exampleEN: I have a happy memory of that day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لدي ذكرى سعيدة من ذلك اليوم.

vocabulary.definition: a planned activity or important thing that happens
vocabulary.exampleEN: The event was in the park.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الحدث كان في الحديقة.

vocabulary.definition: feeling something unexpected happened
vocabulary.exampleEN: I was surprised by the cake.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كنت مندهشًا من الكعكة.

vocabulary.definition: to do something special because of an important event
vocabulary.exampleEN: We celebrated with music and food.
vocabulary.exampleAR: احتفلنا بالموسيقى والطعام.

vocabulary.definition: to make ready before something happens
vocabulary.exampleEN: She prepared a short speech.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حضّرت خطابًا قصيرًا.

vocabulary.definition: to join an activity or be involved
vocabulary.exampleEN: I took part in the school play.
vocabulary.exampleAR: شاركت في مسرحية المدرسة.

vocabulary.definition: to speak to a group at a formal moment
vocabulary.exampleEN: He made a speech at the ceremony.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ألقى خطابًا في الحفل.

vocabulary.definition: to have a happy feeling because of an achievement
vocabulary.exampleEN: I felt proud when my friend clapped.
vocabulary.exampleAR: شعرت بالفخر عندما صفق صديقي.

vocabulary.definition: to use a camera to record a moment
vocabulary.exampleEN: They took a photo after the performance.
vocabulary.exampleAR: التقطوا صورة بعد العرض.

vocabulary.definition: to continue for a period of time
vocabulary.exampleEN: The concert lasted for two hours.
vocabulary.exampleAR: استمر الحفل لمدة ساعتين.

vocabulary.definition: a person you trust and know well
vocabulary.exampleEN: My close friend came to the party.
vocabulary.exampleAR: جاء صديقي المقرب إلى الحفلة.

vocabulary.definition: a large group of people in one place
vocabulary.exampleEN: The crowd cheered loudly.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هتف الحشد بصوت عالٍ.

vocabulary.definition: a book where you write personal events and feelings
vocabulary.exampleEN: She wrote the story in her diary.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كتبت القصة في دفتر يومياتها.

vocabulary.definition: worried or anxious before something important
vocabulary.exampleEN: He was nervous before he spoke.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كان متوترًا قبل أن يتحدث.

vocabulary.definition: to make someone remember something
vocabulary.exampleEN: This photo reminds me of that day.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تذكرني هذه الصورة بذلك اليوم.

grammar.concept: Use past simple verbs to tell what happened and sequencing words (first, then, after that, finally) to show the order of events.
grammar.arabicComparison: اللغة العربية تستخدم فعل الماضي بنفس طريقة سرد الأحداث، لكن كلمات الترتيب (أولًا، ثم، بعد ذلك، أخيرًا) تأتي قبل أو بعد الجملة حسب السياق. حافظ على فعل الماضي للفعل الرئيسي.
grammar.structure: Subject + past simple verb (+ object). Use sequencing words: First..., Then..., After that..., Finally....
grammar.commonError: Mixing past and present tenses (e.g., 'I go to the party and then I saw...') or forgetting irregular past forms (e.g., say → said, go → went).
grammar.exampleEN: First I woke up early. Then I went to the hall. After that I made a speech. Finally, we celebrated with cake.
grammar.exampleAR: أولًا استيقظت مبكرًا. ثم ذهبت إلى القاعة. بعد ذلك ألقيت خطابًا. أخيرًا احتفلنا بالكعكة.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original passage that tells a true-feeling story about one memorable day. The passage describes who was there, the sequence of events, simple actions in past simple (went, saw, felt), and the writer's feelings. It uses clear sequencing words (first, then, after that, finally) and includes at least one short dialogue or direct reaction (e.g., 'I was surprised!'). The text is suitable for A2 learners and shows practical vocabulary from the lesson.
writingPrompt: Write 60–90 words to a friend describing a day you will always remember. Say who was there, what happened (use at least three past simple verbs), and how you felt. Use sequencing words (first, then, after that, finally). Audience: a close friend. Purpose: to share your memory and feelings.

title: Things I have done

outcome.canDo: I can talk about life experiences and short travel stories using the present perfect with ever / never / already / yet.

grammar.topic: Present perfect with ever / never / already / yet
grammar.arabicName: المضارع التام مع ever / never / already / yet
grammar.concept: Use the present perfect (have/has + past participle) to talk about life experiences and actions that connect the past with now. Use 'ever' in questions to ask about experience, 'never' for no experience, 'already' for something done earlier than expected, and 'yet' in negatives/questions when something is expected but not finished.
grammar.arabicComparison: في الإنجليزية، يُستخدم المضارع التام لربط حدث ماضٍ بالحاضر. في العربية غالبًا يُستخدم الماضي للإشارة إلى أفعال منتهية. لذلك بدلاً من قول 'ذهبت أمس' مع المضارع التام، نستخدمه للسؤال عن الخبرات (هل سبق أن...؟).
grammar.structure: Affirmative: Subject + have/has + past participle (+ already). Negative: Subject + have/has + not + past participle OR Subject + have/has + never + past participle. Question: Have/Has + subject + past participle? (Have you ever...?) Use 'yet' in questions/negatives: Have you finished yet? / I haven't finished yet.
grammar.commonError: Using specific past time words (yesterday, last year) with the present perfect. Example error: 'I have visited Paris yesterday.'
grammar.exampleEN: Have you ever climbed a mountain? / I haven't climbed one yet. / I've already visited two countries this year.
grammar.exampleAR: هل سبق أن تسلّقت جبلًا؟ / لم أتسلّق واحدًا بعد. / لقد زرت بلدين بالفعل هذا العام.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original personal account by an adult traveller who lists several life experiences and small achievements. The writer uses the present perfect to connect past events to the present: visiting museums, trying local food, learning a new skill, and a memorable trip with friends. The passage shows questions with 'have you ever', negatives with 'never', and examples of 'already' and 'yet'. It ends with a short reflection: how these experiences changed the writer and a question inviting the reader to share their experiences.
writingPrompt: Write 60–90 words to a friend telling three things you have done in your life or on holiday. Use the present perfect (have/has + past participle) at least three times and include ever, never, already or yet. Keep a friendly tone and ask one question to invite your friend to reply.

grammar.topic: going to, present continuous for arrangements
grammar.concept: Use 'be going to + verb' for intentions or plans you decide to do. Use the present continuous (be + verb-ing) for definite arrangements with a stated time or place.
grammar.arabicComparison: »going to« تستخدم للنية أو الخطة العامة. الحاضر المستمر يستخدم للترتيبات المؤكدة مع وقت أو مكان.
grammar.structure: going to: subject + be + going to + base verb. Present continuous: subject + be + verb-ing (+ time/place).
grammar.commonError: Mixing forms: using 'will' for fixed arrangements or using base verb after 'going to' without 'to' (e.g., I going to go). Also forgetting the -ing after be in present continuous.
grammar.exampleEN: I'm going to call Tom later. / I'm meeting Tom on Saturday at 3 pm.
grammar.exampleAR: سأتصل بتوم لاحقًا (I’m going to call Tom later). / سألتقي بتوم يوم السبت الساعة الثالثة مساءً (I’m meeting Tom on Saturday at 3 pm).

grammar.topic: Advice with should and polite apologies
grammar.concept: Use should + base verb to give simple advice (You should leave early). Use 'I'm sorry' or 'I apologise' + reason (for + -ing / for + noun) to apologise politely.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم عبارات مثل 'من الأفضل أن' للنصيحة و'أعتذر عن...' للاعتذار. should لا يترجم حرفيًا دائماً، وغالبًا يستخدم 'من الأفضل' أو 'ينبغي'.
grammar.structure: Advice: Subject + should + base verb. Apology: I'm sorry / I apologise + (for + noun or for + verb-ing). Example: You should call ahead. I'm sorry for being late.
grammar.commonError: Using 'should' for past apologies (wrong: I should arrived late). Also confusing 'sorry' + infinitive vs 'sorry' + -ing (correct: Sorry for being late / Sorry I was late).
grammar.exampleEN: You should check the bus times. I'm sorry for the delay.
grammar.exampleAR: يجب أن تتحقق من مواعيد الحافلة. أعتذر عن التأخير.

readingBrief: A short original passage (about 130–160 words) set at a small weekday picnic that goes wrong. vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت جدتي دائماً تعد طبقاً خاصاً للعطلات.

vocabulary.definition: to put things to make a place look nice for an event
vocabulary.exampleEN: We decorate the hall with lights and flowers.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نزين القاعة بالأضواء والزهور.

vocabulary.definition: to give portions of food to others at an event
vocabulary.exampleEN: At the party we shared food with our neighbours.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في الحفل شاركنا الطعام مع جيراننا.

grammar.concept: We use 'used to' and 'would' to talk about actions we did regularly in the past. Time expressions (when I was a child, every year, often, in the past) help show these repeated actions. Use the past simple for single completed events.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم غالباً الماضي البسيط مع ظروف زمنية (مثلاً: عندما كنت صغيراً، كل سنة). أحياناً نضيف 'كان' مع الفعل المضارع للدلالة على عادة في الماضي (كان + يفعل)، لكن في الإنجليزية نستخدم 'used to' أو 'would' للأفعال المتكررة.
grammar.structure: Affirmative: subject + used to + base verb (I used to dance). / Also: subject + would + base verb (for repeated actions) (We would sing). Negative: subject + didn't use to + base verb (I didn't use to cook). Question: Did + subject + use to + base verb? (Did you use to visit?). Time words: when I was a child, every year, often, last summer.
grammar.commonError: Students often say 'I used to went' or use present tense 'I go' instead of 'I used to go'. Also confuse 'used to' (past habit) with past simple (single events). In Arabic, learners sometimes translate directly and say the present form.
grammar.exampleEN: When I was young, I used to visit my grandparents every summer and we would light candles together.
grammar.exampleAR: عندما كنت صغيراً، كنت أزور أجدادي كل صيف وكنا نضيء الشموع معاً.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original passage about a woman who remembers the annual village festival from her childhood. The text describes the usual routine: neighbours decorating the square, families bringing a special dish, children wearing costumes, and the local band playing music. It includes past-habit language (used to, would) and clear time expressions (every year, when I was a child, after dinner). The passage shows invitations and polite refusals from relatives and ends with the writer saying how the tradition changed recently.
writingPrompt: Write a 60–90-word message to a friend describing one tradition you used to have in your family and inviting them to a small get-together next weekend. Include at least one past-habit phrase (used to or would) and one time expression (e.g. last year, every summer). Purpose: invite and inform; Audience: a close friend.

title: Study, work, and goals

outcome.canDo: I can say what I have to do, what I need to do, and what I can do to reach my study and work goals.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع أن أقول ما يجب أن أفعله، وما أحتاج أن أفعله، وما أستطيع فعله للوصول إلى أهدافي الدراسية والعملية.
outcome.scenario: You talk with a teacher or colleague about plans for study and work and make a short plan for the week.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تتحدث مع مدرس أو زميل عن خطط الدراسة والعمل وتضع خطة قصيرة للأسبوع.

retrieval.prompt: Think about yesterday: what time did you go to school or work?
retrieval.purpose: Activate simple past time words and routine vocabulary (yesterday, time, go).

retrieval.prompt: Name three places you will go tomorrow (for example: home, shop, school).
retrieval.purpose: Use common places and future plans (tomorrow, go, places).

retrieval.prompt: Who are three people you can ask for help (friend, teacher, manager)?
retrieval.purpose: Recall people vocabulary and asking for help (people, can, ask).

retrieval.prompt: What food do you like before you study or work?
retrieval.purpose: Connect daily routine words (food, like, study, work).

network.anchor: plans and options for study and work
priorLevelLinks: A1: talking about daily routine and time
A1: saying where you go and who you see
network.learningNote: Focus on small, clear steps: use have to for rules and obligations, need to for personal priorities or things you must arrange, and can for ability or permission. Teach short model sentences and practise swapping verbs (study, work, apply).
network.learningNoteArabic: ركز على خطوات صغيرة وواضحة: استخدم 'have to' للالتزامات والقواعد، و'need to' للأولويات الشخصية أو الأشياء التي يجب ترتيبها، و'can' للقدرة أو الإذن. درّب على جمل بسيطة واستبدال الأفعال (study, work, apply).

vocabulary.definition: decide what you want to achieve in a period of time
vocabulary.exampleEN: I set a goal to pass my English test this term.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حددت هدفًا أن أنجح في اختبار اللغة الإنجليزية هذا الفصل.

vocabulary.definition: think about and arrange activities that will help you reach something
vocabulary.exampleEN: I plan my week on Sunday evening.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أخطط لأسبوعي مساء الأحد.

vocabulary.definition: the last day or time to finish something
vocabulary.exampleEN: The deadline for the homework is Friday.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الموعد النهائي للواجب هو يوم الجمعة.

vocabulary.definition: work with fewer hours than a full-time job
vocabulary.exampleEN: She has a part-time job in a café after class.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لديها عمل بدوام جزئي في مقهى بعد الدرس.

vocabulary.definition: send papers or information to ask for a job
vocabulary.exampleEN: I will apply for a job at the library.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأتقدم لوظيفة في المكتبة.

vocabulary.definition: practical time spent working to learn a job
vocabulary.exampleEN: Volunteering gave me good work experience.
vocabulary.exampleAR: التطوع أعطاني خبرة عمل جيدة.

vocabulary.definition: abilities you have that help you do tasks well
vocabulary.exampleEN: Computer skills are useful for many jobs.
vocabulary.exampleAR: المهارات الحاسوبية مفيدة للعديد من الوظائف.

vocabulary.definition: make something better
vocabulary.exampleEN: I want to improve my English speaking.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أريد أن أحسن المحادثة بالإنجليزية.

vocabulary.definition: use your time well to do important things
vocabulary.exampleEN: To finish coursework, I must manage time well.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لإنهاء الأعمال، يجب أن أدير الوقت جيدًا.

vocabulary.definition: a strong wish to achieve something important
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her ambition is to become a teacher.
vocabulary.exampleAR: طموحها أن تصبح معلمة.

vocabulary.definition: do work without pay to help others or gain experience
vocabulary.exampleEN: He volunteers at the local community centre.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هو يتطوع في مركز المجتمع المحلي.

vocabulary.definition: a certificate from a university showing you studied a subject
vocabulary.exampleEN: She wants a degree in business.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ترغب في الحصول على درجة علمية في الأعمال.

vocabulary.definition: the type of work you do over many years
vocabulary.exampleEN: He is building a career in IT.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يبني مسارًا وظيفيًا في تكنولوجيا المعلومات.

vocabulary.definition: show obligation or rules
vocabulary.exampleEN: I have to attend the meeting on Monday.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب أن أحضر الاجتماع يوم الإثنين.

vocabulary.definition: show necessity or personal requirement
vocabulary.exampleEN: I need to study more for the exam.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أحتاج أن أدرس أكثر للامتحان.

grammar.concept: have to is for obligations or external rules, need to is for necessities or personal priorities, and can shows ability or permission.
grammar.arabicComparison: have to للالتزام أو القواعد الخارجية، need to للحاجة أو الأولوية الشخصية، وcan للقدرة أو الإذن.
grammar.structure: Affirmative: subject + have to/need to/can + base verb. Negative: subject + don't have to/don't need to/can't + base verb. Question: Do you have to...? Can you...?
grammar.commonError: Confusing don't have to (no obligation) with mustn't (not allowed), or saying 'I must to' instead of 'I have to' or 'I need to'.
grammar.exampleEN: I have to finish the report. / I need to talk to my tutor. / I can come to class on Friday.
grammar.exampleAR: يجب أن أنهي التقرير. / أحتاج أن أتحدث مع مدرّسي. / أستطيع الحضور إلى الصف يوم الجمعة.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word first-person passage about a student who balances studying and a part-time job. The text describes the student's short-term goals (pass an exam, get more work experience), what they have to do because of rules or work hours, what they need to arrange (study time, sleep), and what they can do to improve (use evening study, ask for help). It includes simple time references (yesterday, tomorrow, this week) and uses have to, need to and can several times. The language is clear, A2 level, and the passage ends with one practical plan for the next seven days.
writingPrompt: Write a short email (60–90 words) to your tutor explaining your study and work goals. Say one thing you have to do this week, one thing you need to change, and one thing you can do to improve. Ask one question for advice. Audience: your tutor. Purpose: inform and ask for help.

title: Technology in daily life

outcome.canDo: I can talk about common devices, say how I use them and make simple future plans using the first conditional.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع التحدث عن الأجهزة الشائعة، وشرح كيف أستخدمها، وصياغة خطط بسيطة للمستقبل باستخدام شرط النوع الأول.
outcome.scenario: You explain to a classmate what devices you use, how you communicate with friends and family, and one change you will make if a problem continues.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تشرح لزميل/زميلة في الصف الأجهزة التي تستخدمها، وكيف تتواصل مع الأصدقاء والعائلة، وتذكر تغييرًا واحدًا ستقوم به إذا استمرّ مشكلة.

retrieval.prompt: Talk about yesterday: What time did you get up, where did you go, and who did you see? Use simple words like time, places, people.
retrieval.purpose: Activate very basic past-time and places vocabulary and speech fluency.

retrieval.prompt: Say what you want and can do tomorrow with technology: I want to check email, I can make a video call, I will go online.
retrieval.purpose: Retrieve common verbs and near-future expressions in an A2 context.

retrieval.prompt: List three places you use a phone (home, work, shop) and one food place where you order online.
retrieval.purpose: Connect places and simple shopping/food vocabulary with device use.

retrieval.prompt: Describe who you like to contact and how: friends, family; do you send a message, call, or video call?
retrieval.purpose: Bring in people and basic communication verbs for speaking practice.

network.learningNote: Focus on real, small changes learners can make with technology (e.g., charge phone, turn off notifications). Teach the form 'If + present, ... will ...' with clear, everyday examples.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركّز على تغييرات واقعية وصغيرة يمكن للمتعلمين القيام بها مع التكنولوجيا (مثل شحن الهاتف، إيقاف الإشعارات). علّم صيغة 'إذا + المضارع، ... سوف/سي ...' بأمثلة يومية وواضحة.

vocabulary.definition: A small computer you carry that makes calls and runs apps.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I check the map on my smartphone when I go to a new place.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أتحقق من الخريطة على هاتفي الذكي عندما أذهب إلى مكان جديد.

vocabulary.definition: A small flat computer with a touch screen, bigger than a phone.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She reads books on her tablet on the bus.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هي تقرأ الكتب على جهازها اللوحي في الحافلة.

vocabulary.definition: A cable or device that gives power to a phone or tablet.
vocabulary.exampleEN: My charger is at home, so my phone is low on battery.
vocabulary.exampleAR: شاحني في المنزل، لذلك بطارية هاتفي منخفضة.

vocabulary.definition: A small program on a phone or tablet for a task, like maps or messages.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I use a translation app when I travel.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أستخدم تطبيق ترجمة عندما أسافر.

vocabulary.definition: A short written note sent on the phone or online.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She sent me a message about the meeting time.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أرسلت لي رسالة عن وقت الاجتماع.

vocabulary.definition: A short alert from an app that gives new information.
vocabulary.exampleEN: My phone gives a notification when I have a new email.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هاتفي يعطي إشعارًا عندما لدي بريد إلكتروني جديد.

vocabulary.definition: Websites and apps where people share posts and talk.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He spends an hour on social media after work.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يقضي ساعة على وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي بعد العمل.

vocabulary.definition: A call where you can see and hear the other person on a screen.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We make a video call with my parents every Sunday.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نجري مكالمة فيديو مع والديّ كل يوم أحد.

vocabulary.definition: Using the bank website or app to check money and pay bills.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I pay bills with online banking because it is fast.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أدفع الفواتير عبر الخدمات المصرفية عبر الإنترنت لأنها سريعة.

vocabulary.definition: A secret word or code to keep an account safe.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Choose a strong password and do not share it.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اختر كلمة مرور قوية ولا تشاركها.

vocabulary.definition: To enter your username and password to use an account.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I log in to my email every morning.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أسجّل الدخول إلى بريدي الإلكتروني كل صباح.

vocabulary.definition: The public name you use to open an online account.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her username is her full name on the learning site.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اسم المستخدم الخاص بها هو اسمها الكامل على موقع التعلم.

vocabulary.definition: To play music from the internet without saving the file.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I stream music while I cook dinner.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أبث الموسيقى أثناء طهي العشاء.

vocabulary.definition: To copy a file from the internet to your device.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Please download the map before you go offline.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الرجاء تنزيل الخريطة قبل أن تكون بدون اتصال.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of time you spend looking at a screen each day.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He tries to reduce his screen time in the evening.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يحاول تقليل وقت الشاشة في المساء.

grammar.concept: We use the first conditional to talk about real possible situations in the future. Use if + present simple, and will + base verb for the result.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم أداة 'إذا' مع فعل في الزمن الحاضر للتحدث عن نتيجة مستقبلية محتملة، ويمكن أن نستخدم المستقبل أو المضارع للفعل الثاني حسب السياق.
grammar.structure: If + present simple, ... will + base verb (If + subject + verb(s), subject + will + verb).
grammar.commonError: Learners often use 'will' in both parts (If I will ...), or they use the present continuous where the present simple is needed.
grammar.exampleEN: If I charge my phone tonight, I will use it all day tomorrow.
grammar.exampleAR: إذا شحنت هاتفي الليلة، فسأستخدمه طوال اليوم غدًا.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original passage where a young person describes a typical day with technology: waking up to a notification, using a smartphone and tablet for work and study, making a video call to family, and checking social media. The text includes simple facts (devices, apps, times) and one clear first conditional sentence about a future change (for example: If I turn off notifications, I will sleep better). The passage shows habits and one plan to improve online balance, with everyday vocabulary and short sentences suitable for A2 learners.
writingPrompt: Write 60–90 words to a friend explaining two habits you will change this week to use technology more safely or happily. Start with one If sentence (first conditional) to show a plan (for example: If I turn off notifications, I will sleep better). Audience: a friend. Purpose: to inform and make a small plan.

title: Media and simple opinions

outcome.canDo: I can talk about films and news and give simple opinions with reasons using because, so and although.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع التحدث عن الأفلام والأخبار وإعطاء آراء بسيطة مع أسباب باستخدام لأن، لذلك، وبالرغم من.
outcome.scenario: You tell a friend about a film you watched and explain why you liked it or not, and you talk about a short news item and your opinion.
outcome.scenarioArabic: تخبر صديقاً عن فيلم شاهدته وتشرح لماذا أعجبك أو لم يعجبك، وتتحدث عن خبر قصير ورأيك فيه.

retrieval.prompt: Yesterday I went to the cinema. Tell me about a time you saw a film.
retrieval.purpose: Activate past-time vocabulary and simple descriptions (yesterday, saw, like).

retrieval.prompt: I like pizza and I go to the town on Saturday. Say what you like and where you go this weekend.
retrieval.purpose: Retrieve likes and places vocabulary (like, go, town, weekend).

retrieval.prompt: Can you tell me who is in your family and one thing they do? (e.g. my brother works).
retrieval.purpose: Bring out people and simple present verbs (people, can, work).

retrieval.prompt: I want news about the weather tomorrow. Say one sentence about tomorrow.
retrieval.purpose: Use simple future/time words (want, tomorrow, weather).

priorLevelLinks: Module 2: Talking about likes and dislikes
network.learningNote: At A2, focus on short, clear reasons. Teach because for reasons, so for results, and although for small contrasts. Give model sentences and short practice: one reason, one contrast.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى A2 ركّز على أسباب قصيرة وواضحة. علّم لأن لذكر السبب، لذلك للنتيجة، وبالرغم من لإظهار التباين. قدّم جمل نموذجية وممارسة قصيرة: سبب واحد وتباين واحد.

vocabulary.definition: A story shown on a screen in a cinema or on TV.
vocabulary.exampleEN: We saw a funny film last night.
vocabulary.exampleAR: شاهدنا فيلماً مضحكاً الليلة الماضية.

vocabulary.definition: A person who plays a part in a film, play or TV show.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The actor played the hero in the film.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لعب الممثل دور البطل في الفيلم.

vocabulary.definition: The person who controls how a film is made.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The director chose the music for the scene.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اختار المخرج الموسيقى للمشهد.

vocabulary.definition: The main events of a story in a film or book.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The plot was easy to follow.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت الحبكة سهلة المتابعة.

vocabulary.definition: A short part of a film or play with action in one place.
vocabulary.exampleEN: My favourite scene is the last one.
vocabulary.exampleAR: مشهد النهاية هو المفضل لدي.

vocabulary.definition: A type of film or book, such as comedy or horror.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I prefer the comedy genre to horror.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أفضل نوع الكوميديا على الرعب.

vocabulary.definition: Information about recent events on TV, radio or online.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I read the news in the morning.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أقرأ الأخبار في الصباح.

vocabulary.definition: Very new and important news that is just happening.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Breaking news: there is a big traffic problem in the city.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أخبار عاجلة: هناك مشكلة مرورية كبيرة في المدينة.

vocabulary.definition: The main title of a news story.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The headline was about a sports win.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كان عنوان الخبر عن فوز رياضي.

vocabulary.definition: A short text or talk that says if a film or book is good.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I read a review before I saw the film.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قرأت مراجعة قبل أن أشاهد الفيلم.

vocabulary.definition: A short opinion about a film that tells if it is good or not.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She wrote a short movie review for the school blog.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كتبت مراجعة فيلم قصيرة لمدونة المدرسة.

vocabulary.definition: To like one thing more than another.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I prefer comedies to horror films.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أفضل الكوميديا على أفلام الرعب.

vocabulary.definition: To look at a film on a screen for its full length.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Do you want to watch a film tonight?
vocabulary.exampleAR: هل تريد مشاهدة فيلم الليلة؟

vocabulary.definition: To make the television start working so you can watch it.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Please turn on the TV; the news starts now.
vocabulary.exampleAR: من فضلك شغّل التلفاز؛ تبدأ الأخبار الآن.

vocabulary.definition: Used to give a reason for something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I liked the film because it was funny.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعجبني الفيلم لأنه كان مضحكاً.

grammar.concept: Use because to give a reason, so to show a result, and although to give a contrast. These connectors help make short opinions with reasons and small surprises.
grammar.arabicComparison: لأن تعطي سبباً، لذلك تظهر نتيجة، وبالرغم من تشير إلى تناقض أو مفاجأة. الترتيب في اللغة الإنجليزية عادة: main clause + connector + clause أو connector + clause + main clause.
grammar.structure: Because + reason (clause). / So + result (clause). / Although + opposite idea (clause). Example: I liked the film because the story was clear. The story was clear, so I enjoyed it. Although it was long, it was interesting.
grammar.commonError: Students often use 'so' when they need 'because', or place 'because' at the end with wrong word order. Also 'although' sometimes needs a comma if it starts a sentence.
grammar.exampleEN: I prefer comedies because they make me laugh, so I felt happy after the film. Although the film was slow, the acting was excellent.
grammar.exampleAR: أفضل الكوميديا لأنها تجعلني أضحك، لذا شعرت بالسعادة بعد الفيلم. بالرغم من أن الفيلم كان بطيئاً، إلا أن التمثيل كان ممتازاً.

readingBrief: A short original passage (about 130–160 words) that describes a person’s weekend with a film and a news story. The writer says which film they watched, gives one clear reason using because, explains a result with so, and adds a small contrast with although. The text uses simple past and present language, mentions a short news headline and the writer's opinion about it, and models useful phrases like 'watch a film' and 'breaking news'. The passage is friendly and suitable for A2 learners.
writingPrompt: Write a 60–90 word message to a friend telling them about a film you watched this week. Say whether you liked it and give one reason with because, one result with so, and one contrast with although. Include a recommendation (yes or no). Audience: a friend. Purpose: inform and give your opinion.

title: Solving everyday problems

outcome.canDo: I can explain a problem, ask for help, accept offers and suggest simple solutions to fix everyday services or repairs.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع شرح المشكلة، طلب المساعدة، قبول العروض واقتراح حلول بسيطة لإصلاح الخدمات أو الأشياء اليومية.
outcome.scenario: You have a broken appliance and need to contact customer service, arrange a repair, and ask for a refund or a discount if needed.
outcome.scenarioArabic: لديك جهاز معطل وتحتاج للاتصال بخدمة العملاء، ترتيب إصلاح، وطلب استرداد الأموال أو خصم إذا لزم الأمر.

retrieval.prompt: Yesterday the washing machine stopped. What time did it break and who was at home?
retrieval.purpose: Recall simple past time words and people (yesterday, time, people).

retrieval.prompt: I want to go to the shop. Where is the nearest place to buy food?
retrieval.purpose: Use places and want/go in a practical question.

retrieval.prompt: Can you call someone to help? I can explain the problem to them.
retrieval.purpose: Use 'can' and people in a request context.

network.learningNote: Teach polite modals (can, could, would) and short offers (I can…, Would you like …) with role plays. Focus on clear steps: describe problem, ask for help, agree a time, note next steps.
network.learningNoteArabic: علّم أساليب الأدب مثل can و could و would وعبارات العرض القصيرة (I can..., Would you like...) من خلال تمارين الأدوار. ركّز على خطوات واضحة: وصف المشكلة، طلب المساعدة، الاتفاق على الوقت، وتدوين الخطوات التالية.

grammar.concept: Use modal verbs and set phrases to make polite requests (Can/Could/Would you...), offers (I can..., Shall I...?), and suggestions (Let's..., How about...?). Choose language that is clear and polite for services and repairs.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم عبارات مثل هل يمكنك؟ أو من فضلك + فعل لطلب المساعدة، وتستخدم كلمات مثل أقترح أو هل نريد لعرض اقتراح. التركيب الإنجليزي يعتمد على أدوات مساعدة مثل can و could و would مع صيغة المصدر.
grammar.structure: Requests: Can/Could/Would you + base verb?  Offers: I can + base verb / Would you like me to + base verb?  Suggestions: Let's + base verb / How about + -ing? / Why don't we + base verb?
grammar.commonError: Learners often use 'can I' when they mean 'can you' (I can = permission for self). Also forgetting 'to' after 'ask' in phrases like 'ask (someone) to do something'.
grammar.exampleEN: Could you send a technician on Friday?  I can stay at home.  How about scheduling the repair at 10 am?
grammar.exampleAR: هل يمكنك إرسال فني يوم الجمعة؟ أستطيع البقاء في المنزل. ماذا عن جدولة الإصلاح الساعة العاشرة صباحًا؟

readingBrief: A 130–160-word original passage about a tenant whose heating stopped working in winter. The text explains how they describe the problem on the phone, speak to customer service, accept an offer for an emergency repair, and ask about a refund because the heater was under warranty. The passage shows short polite requests, an offer from the company, and a final plan for the appointment and follow-up.
writingPrompt: Write a 60–90-word email to a repair company. Audience: customer service. Purpose: explain a recent problem with a broken appliance, request an appointment for repair, and ask politely about a refund or replacement if the item is under guarantee. Use polite requests and one suggestion for a time.

grammar.topic: Talking about future plans: going to, present continuous, will
grammar.arabicName: التحدث عن خطط المستقبل: going to و present continuous و will
grammar.concept: Use 'going to' for intentions or plans you already decided. Use the present continuous (I am meeting) for arrangements with a time or place. Use 'will' for quick decisions, offers, or simple predictions.
grammar.arabicComparison: 'going to' للنية المخططة، present continuous للترتيبات المحددة، 'will' للقرارات الفورية أو التنبؤات البسيطة.
grammar.structure: Subject + am/is/are + going to + verb; Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing (present continuous); Subject + will + verb.
grammar.commonError: Students often use 'will' for planned arrangements (e.g. 'I will meet her at 6') instead of present continuous: 'I am meeting her at 6.'
grammar.exampleEN: I am going to study tonight. / I am meeting my tutor on Monday. / I will help you with vocabulary.
grammar.exampleAR: أنا سأنوي أن أدرس الليلة. / سألتقي بمدرّسي يوم الاثنين. / سأساعدك في المفردات.

readingBrief: A 130–160-word first-person paragraph about a learner who reviews recent progress and chooses a clear next step. The text mentions what the learner practised last week (speaking with a friend, reviewing notes), how they felt (more confident, a little nervous), and one short-term goal (speak for two minutes) plus a long-term plan (prepare for a test next year). It describes specific small actions (practise every day, set a deadline, ask a friend for support) and uses present continuous and 'going to' for plans. The tone is encouraging and honest; useful for reading practice of goal vocabulary and simple future forms.
writingPrompt: Write 60–90 words to your English tutor explaining your next step. Say (1) one short-term goal, (2) one action you will do this week, and (3) how you want to feel. Ask one simple question for advice. Purpose: plan your study and request feedback.
